quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield should:

options.text: Block your view to both sides.
Fit so tight that eyeglasses cannot fit underneath.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: A helmeted rider is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets, no matter how fast they are going.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: Signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: Usually, you should keep a minimum following distance of _____ .
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum following distance of two seconds. Increase it to at least three seconds when riding in poor weather or other unsafe conditions.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride:

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: When riding at night you should:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see better.
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be flexible with your lane position when riding at night.

questions.question: Do not change gears on railroad tracks because:

options.text: Other drivers may not expect you to change gears.
The uneven surface makes shifting gears harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle could stall while you are on the tracks.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When it is raining, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery when rain first starts. Oil from cars has not washed away yet. The safest choice is to ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the best option.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive any motor vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is slippery when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is usually the safest option.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: Park at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Park at a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Park like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
Park at the left edge of the space so other drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: If the road is slippery, what should you do?

options.text: Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead.
Follow the vehicle ahead more closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: On slippery pavement, your motorcycle needs more distance to stop. Increase your following distance to at least three seconds behind the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run parallel to the road, how should you cross?
questions.correctAnswerText: Cross at a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks at least at a 45-degree angle. Make a quick, sharp turn to avoid the tracks catching your tire and throwing you off balance.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, what headlight should you use?

options.text: Switch between high and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass.
Move to one side of the lane so they can pass within the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Change lanes if you can, or slow down to let them go ahead. Speeding up will not help—they will just tailgate you at the higher speed.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip opposite to the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side of your turn. Press the opposite handgrip to return to your original direction after you clear the hazard.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Slow down and approach the dog. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane
Either the left or right side

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you farthest from opening car doors, people stepping between cars, and cars pulling out of spaces.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, how should you lean?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle only and keep your body straight.
Keep the motorcycle straight and lean your body.
Lean both the motorcycle and your body.
Do not lean your body or the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the motorcycle only and keep your body straight.
questions.explanation: In a normal turn, lean the motorcycle and your body together. In a slow, tight turn, lean only the motorcycle and keep your body upright to stay balanced.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Block all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit securely to your face.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, allow clear side vision, fit securely, allow air to flow to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:

options.text: Not needed if you wear a helmet.
Not needed if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed along with a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Hearing protection can help while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: Small vehicles can look ______ and seem to move ______ than they really are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, slower
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and seem slower than they actually are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge a small vehicle's real location and speed.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load, you should adjust the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, set your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the levels recommended for that weight.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side closest to the passing driver increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may make the passing driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is usually safe for motorcyclists unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided because other parts of the lane are safer.
Improves traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars drips in the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area gives enough grip for motorcycles to ride safely. The strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side and stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles and at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white background and black lettering show traffic rules like speed limits. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.
questions.correctAnswerText: Five times
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to get a serious head injury in a crash.

questions.question: When riding at night, keep a minimum distance of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distance. Keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. You may need extra time to notice a stopped vehicle and to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors and you are not familiar with them, you should practice using them because:

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It can be hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view behind you. They also make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Practice using your mirrors if your motorcycle has convex mirrors.

questions.question: When riding under normal conditions, you should stay at least this distance behind other vehicles:
questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Proper riding clothing offers all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothing protects you from injury in a crash and from weather. It prevents discomfort rather than causing it.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees they will yield to you.
Does not mean they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver will yield to you. A driver can look directly at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: The best way to brake in a straight line is to:

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: The best way to brake in a straight line is to use both the front and rear brakes at the same time. Do not lock either wheel.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: Keep close together as a group so others can see you. Give each rider enough space to move safely. Riding in pairs does not give riders enough room to maneuver.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, they often seem to be:

options.text: Traveling faster than they actually are.
Traveling slower than they actually are.
Not moving when they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traveling faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's small size can make it appear to be going faster than it really is.

questions.question: Before a passenger rides with you, instruct them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay far away from you.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to board after the engine starts. They should sit forward and hold onto the handholds or your waist. They should keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.question: To stop other drivers from sharing your lane, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Make eye contact with other drivers.
Not let other vehicles pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to share it. Motorcycles need the full lane width to operate safely.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, you should not:

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing down.
Use both brakes when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing down.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges, as these are more slippery.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to ride faster than the others, what should the group do?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet up at a designated spot later.
Speed up to keep up with that rider.
Split up and let every rider go their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet up at a designated spot later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster, let them ride ahead. Plan to meet at a specific place later.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It takes up less space on the highway.
The group is easier to see.
The group is less likely to get separated.
Riders reach their destination faster in a close group than in a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders reach their destination faster in a close group than in a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a close group takes up less space, is easier to see, and is less likely to get split up at traffic lights. However, it does not make you reach your destination faster.

questions.question: When going through a curve, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of your lane.
Always stay on the left side of your lane.
Always stay on the right side of your lane.
Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Conditions can change quickly. Be ready to move your lane position when needed. The best way through a curve may not match the road's curve.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Ask other friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: Do not suggest they drive on less-crowded roads. Instead, arrange other transportation, get friends to help stop them, or keep them from driving until they are sober.

questions.question: How does motorcycle stopping distance compare to car stopping distance?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Normally, motorcycles and cars need about the same distance to stop. Wet or slippery roads make it harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be seen easily.
Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Is recommended because a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
Is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of your lane where the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: The best lane position:

options.text: Blocks your view of the road ahead.
Places you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no one best lane position. Change your position as conditions change. Choose a position that helps you see and be seen, avoids wind from other vehicles, and keeps you out of blind spots.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Motorcycle windshields:

options.text: Work as well as a face shield.
Do not protect your eyes from wind.
Protect you from items thrown by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good replacement for a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, the rider should:

options.text: Keep their body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean away from the motorcycle and the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while leaning their body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with the motorcycle at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
